questions.question_text: A patient asks you about a recent newspaper report on the neuregulin-1 gene and psychiatric disorder. You explain to her that the most likely psychiatric link is with which one of the following disorders?
questions.explanation: Linkage studies have shown a relation between schizophrenia and the neuregulin-1 gene.

questions.question_text: Transfer of information from the DNA molecule to the primary RNA is called:
questions.explanation: Transcription is the transfer of information from DNA to tRNA. Translation is the process of producing proteins from messenger RNA.

questions.question_text: Regarding autosomal-dominant inheritance, which of the following statements is false?

options.text: The phenotypic trait is present in all individuals carrying the dominant allele
Disorder is transmitted only if both parents are homozygous
Males and females can be affected

correct_answer.text: Disorder is transmitted only if both parents are homozygous

correct_answers.text: Disorder is transmitted only if both parents are homozygous

questions.explanation: The phenotype is transmitted only if both parents are homozygous in autosomal-recessive conditions, while in autosomal-dominant conditions it can be transmitted even if one parent is heterozygous.

questions.question_text: In X-linked recessive inheritance, all of the following statements can be true, except:

options.text: Males with the abnormal allele manifest the phenotypic trait
Both the X chromosomes need to have the abnormal allele in a female for the trait to be manifested
The X-linked recessive traits are rarer than the X-linked dominant traits

questions.explanation: Males inherit their X chromosome from their mother, hence male-to-male transmission cannot occur. X-linked recessive disorders are rare.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a technique used in molecular genetics?
questions.explanation: Molecular genetics are used to find the genes for specific diseases. For this, the DNA has to be cut or spliced at specific areas. Cutting, splicing, blotting and recombination are all techniques used in molecular genetics.

questions.question_text: All of the following disorders are due to trisomy, except:
questions.explanation: Down syndrome relates to trisomy 21. Edwards syndrome relates to trisomy 18. Patau syndrome relates to trisomy 13.

questions.question_text: All of the following are X-linked dominant disorders, except:
questions.explanation: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal-dominant disorder. There are 46 autosomal chromosomes and any deformity in them usually is prevalent equally in both sexes.

questions.question_text: The likelihood of a person with a particular genotype presenting with the associated phenotype is called:
questions.explanation: Concordance is seen in particular in studies of twins where both co-twins show the same disorder. A proband or index case is the affected person in a family risk study.

questions.question_text: All of the following are X-linked recessive disorders, except:
questions.explanation: Hurler syndrome is autosomal recessive.

questions.question_text: The prevalence rate of Alzheimer's dementia over the age of 95 is:
questions.explanation: The prevalence of dementia increases with age. Around a third of the population over the age of 85 years suffer from dementia.

questions.question_text: If concordance for a psychiatric disorder is higher in monozygotic twins than in dizygotic twins, a genetic component is presumed; the greater the difference in concordance, the greater the ...:
questions.explanation: Heritability is the difference in the concordance between monozygotic twins and dizygotic twins rather than the concordance in any one type of twins. Penetrance is the likelihood of a person with a genotype known to cause a phenotype presenting that characteristic.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding genetic studies of personality disorders?

options.text: Heritability of antisocial behaviour is seen more in adults
Shared environmental factors are more important in the aetiology of antisocial behaviour in children and adolescents than in adults
Adoptees separated at birth from persistent antisocial parents have higher rates of antisocial personality behaviour than do adoptees whose parents are not antisocial
Antisocial personality disorder is diagnosed more often in men than women
Biological parents of children who are not antisocial show more antisocial behaviour than do the biological parents of antisocial children

correct_answer.text: Biological parents of children who are not antisocial show more antisocial behaviour than do the biological parents of antisocial children

correct_answers.text: Biological parents of children who are not antisocial show more antisocial behaviour than do the biological parents of antisocial children

questions.explanation: These are all findings from important studies on personality disorders except for choice e, which should have been that parents of antisocial children show more antisocial behaviour than do the biological parents of children who are not antisocial.

questions.question_text: A nitrogenous base (e.g. adenine) and sugar (e.g. ribose or deoxyribose) give rise to:
questions.explanation: A nucleoside is the nitrogenous base and sugar. A nucleotide is a nucleoside plus a phosphate. DNA and RNA are polymers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding DNA replication?

options.text: Synthesis can occur only in the 50–30direction
DNA replication ends at a replication fork
Hydrogen bond holding the two DNA strands are cut by ligase
Polymerase helps in binding the Okazaki fragments
Uracil is used instead of thymine in DNA

correct_answer.text: Synthesis can occur only in the 50–30direction

correct_answers.text: Synthesis can occur only in the 50–30direction

questions.explanation: DNA strand synthesis always occur in the 50–30direction. Synthesis occurs in the other strand by production of Okazaki fragments. DNA ligase binds the Okazaki fragments together. Thymine is the nucleotide used instead of uracil in DNA. Uracil is the nucleotide used in RNA.

questions.question_text: Regarding DNA synthesis, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Synthesis on the leading strand is by DNA polymerase d
Synthesis on the lagging strand is by DNA polymerase a
Okazaki fragments are synthesized from the leading strand
Synthesis of DNA is called semi-discontinuous
Synthesis of DNA is called semi-conservative

correct_answer.text: Okazaki fragments are synthesized from the leading strand

correct_answers.text: Okazaki fragments are synthesized from the leading strand

questions.explanation: Synthesis of DNA is semi-conservative, as on both identical daughter duplexes it has an original strand. Also, it is semi-discontinuous, as DNA is formed discontinuously on the lagging strand. Okazaki fragments are produced from the lagging strand and not from the leading strand.

questions.question_text: Genetic studies include which of the following:
questions.explanation: Family studies, twin studies and adoption studies are the conventional methods of genetic study, while modern methods include recombinant fraction, restriction endonucleases and linkage analysis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding autosomal abnormalities?

options.text: Most cases of Down syndrome are due to translocation of genetic material between chromosome 21 and another
Prader–Willi syndrome is due to partial deletion of the short arm of chromosome 15
Cri-du-chat syndrome is due to deletion on the short arm of chromosome 5
Deletion on chromosome 13 can lead to Wilms' tumour

correct_answer.text: Cri-du-chat syndrome is due to deletion on the short arm of chromosome 5

correct_answers.text: Cri-du-chat syndrome is due to deletion on the short arm of chromosome 5

questions.explanation: The most common type of Down syndrome (95%) arises because of meiotic non-dysjunction; less than 5% is due to translocation. Edwards syndrome is due to trisomy 18. Trisomy 13 leads to Patau syndrome. Prader–Willi syndrome is due to partial deletion of the long arm of chromosome 15. Deletion on chromosome 11 may lead to Wilms' tumour.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding men with Klinefelter syndrome, except:

options.text: The phenotypic male has an extra Y chromosome
They may have a disproportionate body shape

correct_answer.text: The phenotypic male has an extra Y chromosome

correct_answers.text: The phenotypic male has an extra Y chromosome

questions.explanation: Males with Klinefelter syndrome usually present with small testes and low testosterone level, and are hence infertile. They usually have gynaecomastia and elongated limbs. Often their IQ is normal.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding females with Turner syndrome?

options.text: They can be diagnosed by buccal mucosa cell chromosomal analysis
They usually have associated cardiovascular defects
Craniofacial abnormalities include micrognathia, low-set ears and downward-slanting palpebral fissures

questions.explanation: Turner syndrome is diagnosed by buccal mucosal cell chromosomal analysis showing XO. Girls with Turner syndrome usually have short stature. Cardiovascular defects include atrial septal defects and coarctation of the aorta.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding fragile X syndrome?

options.text: It is also called Martin–Bell–Renpenning syndrome
Most people with the syndrome have normal IQ
Speech is usually high pitched and often nasal
People with the syndrome have short stature
Males with the syndrome present with macro-orchidism

correct_answer.text: Most people with the syndrome have normal IQ

correct_answers.text: Most people with the syndrome have normal IQ

questions.explanation: Fragile X syndrome is the most common cause of mental retardation in males after Down syndrome. All the others are features of fragile X syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an autosomal-dominant syndrome with characteristic features of tall stature, long slim limbs and arachnodactyly?
questions.explanation: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal-dominant disorder. There are 46 autosomal chromosomes and any deformity in them usually is prevalent equally in both sexes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Capping and polyadenylation are types of post-translational processing
The anti-codon is seen on the tRNA
AUG is also known as the termination codon
Transcription follows translation in gene expression

correct_answer.text: The anti-codon is seen on the tRNA

correct_answers.text: The anti-codon is seen on the tRNA

questions.explanation: RNA splicing, capping and polyadenylation are all types of post-transcriptional processing. Transcription occurs in the 50–30direction. AUG is the initiation codon. Translation occurs after transcription.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding Duchenne muscular dystrophy, except:

options.text: It is an X-linked recessive disease
It is mainly seen in females
Symptoms are usually manifested before the age of 6 years
The disorder is caused by a mutation in the DMD gene
In affected individuals, creatine phosphokinase-MM levels in the bloodstream are extremely high

correct_answer.text: It is mainly seen in females

correct_answers.text: It is mainly seen in females

questions.explanation: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is mainly seen in males since it is an X-linked disorder and females are usually carriers.

questions.question_text: 'Artificial embryo twinning' and 'somatic cell nuclear transfer' are procedures specifically related to:
questions.explanation: Both artificial embryo twinning and somatic cell nuclear transfer are types of cloning used in laboratories. Artificial embryo twinning is very similar to the natural process of twin formation.

questions.question_text: What are the missing words? RNA contains base ...in place of base ...in DNA.
questions.explanation: One of the main differences between RNA and DNA is in the pyramidine bases. RNA has uracil in place of thymine as the pyramidine base in the nucleotides.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding Smith–Lemli–Opitz syndrome (SLOS)?

options.text: It is a metabolic disorder caused by a mutation on chromosome 11
The disease mainly pertains to hampered synthesis of an enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis
SLOS is inherited in an autosomal-dominant pattern
Cleft palate and polydactyly are symptoms related to SLOS
People with SLOS usually present with mental retardation

correct_answer.text: SLOS is inherited in an autosomal-dominant pattern

correct_answers.text: SLOS is inherited in an autosomal-dominant pattern

questions.explanation: The mutation occurs in the DHCR7 (7-dehydrocholesterol reductase) gene on chromosome 11. The autosomal-recessive disorder, which to date has no cure, can be supported only with cholesterol supplementation, owing to an increase in life expectancy. Those affected, however, are mentally retarded.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding phenylketonuria (PKU)?

options.text: Individuals affected always have a normal IQ
PKU is due to a mutation on chromosome 12
The main pathology is due to excess phenylalanine
PKU can be detected by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) or the Guthrie test
It is inherited as an autosomal-recessive disease

correct_answer.text: Individuals affected always have a normal IQ

correct_answers.text: Individuals affected always have a normal IQ

questions.explanation: Phenylketonuria is associated with low IQ.

questions.question_text: Classical galactosaemia affects one in every how many newborn infants?
questions.explanation: The incidence of classical galactosaemia is 55 000 to 60 000.

questions.question_text: People with cystic fibrosis inherit a defective gene called CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) on which chromosome?
questions.explanation: The defective gene in cystic fibrosis is on chromosome 7.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency?

options.text: It is a common genetic cause of liver disease in children
It usually manifests in the fifth decade
It is easily differentiated from other respiratory abnormalities like emphysema, asthma, etc.
Alpha-1-antitrypsin is synthesized mainly in the lungs

correct_answer.text: It is a common genetic cause of liver disease in children

correct_answers.text: It is a common genetic cause of liver disease in children

questions.explanation: Alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency is one of the most common genetic causes of liver disease in children.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has the lowest heritability estimate?
questions.explanation: Heritability is the proportion of the liability to a disorder in a population that is accounted for by genetic effects; it is usually expressed as a percentage. It is highest for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder (80%); for alcohol problem or dependence it is 60%; for major depression and panic disorder it is 40% for each; and for generalized anxiety disorder it is 35%.

questions.question_text: Regarding genetic variations, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Polymorphisms or allelic variants occur on average every 1000 nucleotides across the whole genome
Most polymorphisms involve a change in a single nucleotide
Most polymorphisms are clinically significant with functional correlates
In linkage studies, a LOD score of more than 3 is conventionally taken as reasonable evidence for linkage
All chromosomes can be studied in genome wide linkage scans

correct_answer.text: Most polymorphisms are clinically significant with functional correlates

correct_answers.text: Most polymorphisms are clinically significant with functional correlates

questions.explanation: Most polymorphisms have no known significance, especially those that are silent or conservative substitutions.

questions.question_text: Regarding genetic polymorphisms in psychiatry, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The APOE4 variant gene on chromosome 19 is identified as a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease
COMT Val158Met polymorphism is identified as a risk factor for schizophrenia
COMT Val158Met polymorphism may predict response to antipsychotic drugs
5-HT transporter gene polymorphism predisposes to depression following early life events

questions.explanation: In APOE4 in Alzheimer's disease and COMT Val158Met in schizophrenia the variants are coding, but in most genetic variations in psychiatric disorders they are non-coding. The non-coding variants may affect processing of mRNA.

questions.question_text: The Papez circuit includes:

options.text: The anterior nucleus of the thalamus

questions.explanation: The limbic system (Papez circuit) was described by James Papez in 1937. In addition to atod, the cingulate gyrus is also part of it.

questions.question_text: Regarding neuronal migration, all the following statements are true, except:

options.text: It mainly occurs in the first 6 months of gestation
It is guided by radially oriented astrocytic glial fibres
Heterotopic neurons within the frontal lobe and failure to complete axonal path finding are thought to be associated with pathology in schizophrenia
The peak of synaptogenesis occurs in gestation
In normal development the subplate neurons degenerate

correct_answer.text: The peak of synaptogenesis occurs in gestation

correct_answers.text: The peak of synaptogenesis occurs in gestation

questions.explanation: The peak of synaptogenesis occurs in the first two postnatal years; the thalamic axon first synapses to the subplate neurons, and in normal development the axon detaches from the subplate neurons and proceeds superficially to synapse on the true cortical cell. In normal development, the subplate neurons degenerate and the presence of heterotopic neurons within the frontal lobe and failure to complete axonal path finding are thought to be associated with pathology in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a criterion for a neurotransmitter?

options.text: It is synthesized in the neuron
It is present in the presynaptic neuron and is released on depolarization in physiologically significant amounts
When administered exogenously as a drug, it should mimic the effects of the endogenous neurotransmitter
A mechanism in the neurons or synaptic cleft acts to remove or deactivate it

questions.explanation: Substances that have been shown to meet only a few of the criteria are referred to as putative neurotransmitters.

questions.question_text: Regarding the biochemical properties of dopamine, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Monoamine oxidase (MAO) is located on the outer mitochondrial membrane, principally in the presynaptic terminal
Catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) is the principal enzyme metabolizing dopamine
The primary metabolite of dopamine is homovanillic acid (HVA)
The rate-limiting step in the synthesis of any of the catecholamines is catalysed by tyrosine kinase

correct_answer.text: Catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) is the principal enzyme metabolizing dopamine

correct_answers.text: Catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) is the principal enzyme metabolizing dopamine

questions.explanation: Monoamine oxidase (MAO) is the principal enzyme metabolizing dopamine; catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) metabolizes dopamine to a lesser extent.

questions.question_text: Peptide neurotransmitters include:
questions.explanation: Peptide receptors are members of the seven-transmembrane domain, G-protein linked family. Almost all peptide neurotransmitters coexist in storage vesicles with other neurotransmitters.

questions.question_text: Regarding amino acid neurotransmitters, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: GABA is an inhibitory amino acid
Glutamate is an excitatory amino acid
Benzodiazepines, barbiturates and several anticonvulsants act through GABAergic mechanisms

questions.explanation: GABA and glutamate receptors are thought to be associated with anxiety disorders and schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of GABA?

options.text: It does not cross the blood–brain barrier
The highest concentrations are in the midbrain and the diencephalons
It is synthesized from glutamate by the rate-limiting enzyme glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD)
Its synthesis requires pyridoxine as a cofactor

questions.explanation: GABA is metabolized by enzyme GABA transaminase and is the primary neurotransmitter in the intrinsic neurons that function as local mediators for the inhibitory feedback loops.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding GABA receptors?

options.text: The GABA Breceptor is G-protein coupled
GABA Aand GABA Care directly acting, ligand-gated chloride ion channels that increase membrane polarization
The GABA Bagonist baclofen is used to treat spasticity
The GABA Areceptor antagonists bicuculline and picrotoxin induce seizures

questions.explanation: Because GABA is thought to suppress seizure activity, anxiety and mania, considerable effort has been devoted to synthesizing drugs that potentiate GABA activity.

questions.question_text: All of the following anticonvulsants are correctly paired with their actions on GABA, except:
questions.explanation: Gabapentin is a GABA derivative and an effective anticonvulsant, but it has no activity on GABA receptors or GABA transporters.

questions.question_text: Glutamate is the primary neurotransmitter in all of the following areas of the brain, except:

options.text: The intrinsic neurons for the inhibitory feedback loops
The cells of the hippocampal molecular layer and entorhinal cortex

correct_answer.text: The intrinsic neurons for the inhibitory feedback loops

correct_answers.text: The intrinsic neurons for the inhibitory feedback loops

questions.explanation: Glutamate is an excitatory amino acid; glycine (an inhibitory amino acid) is the primary neurotransmitter in intrinsic neurons for the inhibitory feedback loops.

questions.question_text: Glutamate receptors include:
questions.explanation: There are five types of glutamate receptors: NMDA receptors; AMPA (alpha amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid) receptors; kinate receptors; AP4 (1,2 amino-4-phosphorobutyrate) receptors; and CAPD (trans-1-aminocyclopentane-1-3-dicarboxylic acid) receptors.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding NMDA receptors, except:

options.text: They allow the passage of sodium, potassium and calcium
Their voltage-gated channels open only when bound by two molecules of glutamate and one molecule of glyceine
NMDA receptor channels open when the membrane potential rises above 65 mV
They are blocked by physiological concentrations of magnesium
They are blocked by phencyclidine and dizocilpine

correct_answer.text: NMDA receptor channels open when the membrane potential rises above 65 mV

correct_answers.text: NMDA receptor channels open when the membrane potential rises above 65 mV

questions.explanation: NMDA receptor channels open when the membrane potential rises above265 mV .

questions.question_text: Regarding glutamate receptors, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: NMDA receptor antagonists have been shown to prevent the formation of memory
AMPA and kinate receptors share their principal effect with NMDA receptors
The AP4 receptor is an excitatory autoreceptor
The ACPD receptor is a metabotropic receptor
The ACPD receptor is G-protein coupled and exerts its effects through the phosphoinositol second messenger system

correct_answer.text: The AP4 receptor is an excitatory autoreceptor

correct_answers.text: The AP4 receptor is an excitatory autoreceptor

questions.explanation: The AP4 receptor is an inhibitory autoreceptor.

questions.question_text: Regarding pathophysiology associated with glutamate, all of the following statements are correct, except:

options.text: Glutamate release is inhibited by nicotine
Excessive stimulation of glutamate receptors may cause excessive intraneuronal concentration of calcium and nitric oxide
Psychotomimetic effects of phencyclidine on glutamate receptors may explain the pathophysiology associated with schizophrenia
Dopamine and glutamate were observed to have opposing effects
Sensitivity of nigral dopamine-containing neurons to excitotoxicity may explain the involvement of glutamates in the pathophysiology associated with Parkinsonism

correct_answer.text: Glutamate release is inhibited by nicotine

correct_answers.text: Glutamate release is inhibited by nicotine

questions.explanation: Nicotine stimulates the release of glutamate.

questions.question_text: The blood-oxygen-level dependent (BOLD) sequence of the brain is obtained by:
questions.explanation: Functional magnetic resonance imaging does not detect brain activity per se, but detects blood flow and levels of oxygenated haemoglobin in the blood as BOLD signals.

questions.question_text: 123I-ioflupane-SPECT (single-photon emission computerized tomography) DaTSCAN is useful in the diagnosis of:
questions.explanation: DaTSCAN involves injection of an intravenous radiolabelled ligand of the presynaptic dopamine amine transporter (DaT) followed by SPECT using a gamma-camera; it evaluates the amount of presynaptic dopamine transporters in the striatum.

questions.question_text: Parkinson's disease occurs in a rare autosomal-dominant form caused by mutations in which of the following genes?
questions.explanation: There is also an autosomal-recessive form due to mutations in several other gene, including PARKIN, DJ1 and PNK1.
